DayOne CEO Jamie Khoo says: “For DayOne, we think about customers’ requirements in scalable land, power, energy and other critical resources from the earliest stages of development. Partnering with Sembcorp gives us an opportunity to explore integrated data centre and energy solutions to support DayOne’s continued expansion across the region.”

title: South Korea's FuriosaAI quadruples value to US$2.9 bil in Nvidia chase
article:
(Oct 29): South Korean artificial intelligence (AI) chip start-up FuriosaAI quadrupled its valuation to US$2.9 billion ($3.7 billion) in a fresh funding round, bolstering its bid to challenge the likes of Nvidia Corp.

The Seoul-based upstart said on Thursday it raised US$620 million in a Series D round from investors including US-based Infinitum Partners. South Korea’s National Growth Fund contributed US$280 million and international investors US$110 million, with Jericho Capital, Worldline Capital, Singapore’s QUDA Capital and Abu Dhabi-based NeoFort Holding among backers.

Investors are hunting for alternatives for Nvidia chips that dominate AI data centres, seeking more energy-efficient silicon. That shift centres on inference — generating outputs from trained AI models — which is emerging as one of the industry’s primary cost battlegrounds as rising demand boosts power needs.

Founded in 2017, FuriosaAI began mass production of RNGD — pronounced “renegade” — chips in January and is working with Broadcom Inc on a third-generation accelerator targeting large-scale AI infrastructure. The start-up is betting that its chip architecture, designed to minimise energy-intensive data movement, will help it gain ground in the Nvidia-led market. Its previous round last year valued the company at US$735 million.

FuriosaAI is engaged with a large number of customers in the Asia-Pacific region and Middle East, chief executive officer June Paik said in an interview on Bloomberg Television on Thursday. “We see strong demand and opportunities as we are scaling our business globally.”

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co is producing 20,000 RNGD accelerators this year, with the South Korean start-up aiming to more than double output to over 40,000 units in 2027. Samsung SDS, LG Group and South Korean AI start-up Upstage are among those that are using the chips.

See also: Nvidia-backed firm launches US$3.1 bil GPU loan in market

Existing backers Naver Corp, Korea Development Bank, DSC Investment, Nextrans and Kakao Investment also joined the financing round, while the Export-Import Bank of Korea made its first direct start-up investment in FuriosaAI.

title: Air Liquide’s sales grow on sustained AI-related demand
article:
(Oct 29): Air Liquide SA revenue grew to its highest in nearly four years, propelled by increased demand in its artificial intelligence (AI)-exposed unit.

Third-quarter revenue in the electronics business, which supplies ultra-pure specialty gases and advanced materials to semiconductor factories grew 12% on a comparable basis. Overall sales rose to €7.3 billion, ahead of the €7.1 billion analysts had expected.

Paris-listed Air Liquide is one of the three main providers of industrial gases, along with Linde Plc and Air Products and Chemicals Inc, and supplies industrial gases and advanced materials used in chipmaking.

Growth for the unit came mostly from Asia, with momentum for carrier gases driven by the start-up and ramp-up of new production units, particularly in China, the group said in a Thursday statement. Demand for some of the unit’s other products came from South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Japan.

The company said it invested over €170 million in Japan for the supply ultra-pure gases to “support market momentum in semiconductors and AI.”

Investments in the electronics business to support AI almost doubled in the first nine months of the year compared to the full year 2025, the company said.

The company also said it launched the first €1 billion tranche of its share buyback programme announced earlier this month, seeking to assuage pressure from Elliott Investment Management. It reiterated its financial guidance.

title: EU climate chief rules out fresh finance pledges at COP31
article:
(Oct 29): The European Union’s climate chief, Wopke Hoekstra, said talks on new climate finance commitments at this year’s United Nations COP31 summit are “dead in the water” after two years of stalled progress on cutting global emissions.

The 27-member bloc is already the biggest provider of climate finance globally, increasing its spending by €5 billion to €33 billion in 2025, according to figures from the European Commission. But EU officials increasingly feel that other countries are failing to match that financial support with more ambitious emissions-cutting contributions.

“Let’s not fall into the trap to have endless new rounds on financing,” Hoekstra said in an interview. “The problem needs something much more fundamental.”

His comments allude to a key area of tension as almost 200 nations assemble in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov 9 for two-week discussions on how to tackle climate change. The summits frequently expose divisions between developed countries pushing for faster emissions cuts and developing nations seeking financial support to transition to cleaner economies and protect themselves against increasingly extreme weather.

The world is now all but certain to fly past the Paris Agreement’s landmark goal of limiting global warming below 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, according to the United Nations Environment Programme. To achieve even the “lowest possible” overshoot scenario, countries would have to slash emissions by 18% this decade. Even if all national climate plans are implemented, they’d only fall by 6% by 2035, according to a report this week.

See also: Europe’s heat-parched land poses risks for next year’s crops

Turkey, the host of COP31, has said a key goal of this year’s summit is to secure a global commitment to increase the electricity’s share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. Discussions will also take place on extending a so-called mitigation work programme to discuss how best to cut emissions. Brazil, last year’s host, is expected to present roadmaps for transitioning away from fossil fuels and curbing deforestation.

Two years ago, at COP29, developed countries agreed to boost public climate finance to US$300 billion by 2035. Last year, countries struck a deal to triple adaptation finance by that date. With the US under President Donald Trump no longer participating in the COP process, much of that burden is set to fall on European nations.

“Any conversation on new fresh money is dead in the water,” Hoekstra said. “At least to the extent that we are the ones who should be providing it.”

See also: Chronic heat risk in Europe draws warning from Swiss Re

That’s a thinly-veiled reference to the likes of China, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states, which argue that responsibility for providing climate finance should rest with countries that industrialised first.

Hoekstra said that relations with Beijing will remain challenging at COP31. While both sides agree broadly on electrification and the gravity of climate change, there are still questions over China “dumping” clean technologies on the EU and the country’s build-out of coal-fired power stations.

For its part, the Asian nation has fiercely criticised the EU’s carbon border levy, which imposes a charge on imports of certain products from countries with less stringent climate rules.

“There is a range of complications on the table,” Hoekstra said. “It’s a mixed bag at best.”

title: Jio Platforms adds US$36 bil in value after India IPO surge
article:
(Oct 29): Jio Platforms Ltd has added almost US$36 billion in market value in two trading sessions, extending its blistering run after India’s biggest-ever initial public offering and underscoring investor appetite for direct exposure to the telecom and digital-services giant.

Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd’s unit jumped as much as 5.1% Thursday, building on a nearly 27% surge in their trading debut. The gains lifted Jio’s market value to about US$144 billion, compared with roughly US$108 billion at its IPO price, cementing its position as India’s second-most valuable listed company.

Attention now turns to Jio’s quarterly earnings on Friday, which will offer a fresh of whether the company can justify its rich valuation. Investors will be watching for signals from Akash Ambani, the eldest son of Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani, on the outlook for revenue and profit growth as Jio seeks to capitalise on a customer base of more than 500 million.

title: Hyundai's profit beats estimates on North America, India growth
article:
(Oct 29): Hyundai Motor Co reported better-than-expected earnings for the third quarter as the automaker benefited from strong demand for its cars in North America and India.

The manufacturer’s operating profit rose 5.5% to 2.68 trillion won in the period, Hyundai said on Thursday. That topped analyst estimates for 2.61 trillion won. Revenue fell 3.4% to 45.1 trillion won.

The performance was underpinned by Hyundai’s best-ever third quarter in the US, where rising gas prices strengthened sales of hybrid models including the Santa Fe sport utility vehicle and the Sonata sedan. Retail sales in India, a key future growth market, rose 9.5% in the period.

The gains helped Hyundai offset falling sales in Europe and China, as well as negative currency impacts. South Korea’s won hit a two-year high last week, reversing declines from earlier this year. That weighed on margins as the company generates most of its revenue overseas. Hyundai also faced labour strikes in July that crimped production.

The results are much-needed relief for Hyundai as it navigates an uncertain business environment. China’s auto market has been shrinking for months, while the removal of EV subsidies in the US has hurt sales of the group’s fully electric models. Brands led by BYD Co are also expanding in Europe, winning share with competitively priced hybrid models.

title: Geely's profit climbs as rising exports offset China slump
article:
(Oct 29): Geely Automobile Holdings Ltd’s profit climbed in the third quarter as surging exports helped the carmaker offset fierce competition in China.

Net income rose by more than a quarter to 4.84 billion yuan in the period, Geely said on Thursday. Revenue also climbed as the company’s vehicle exports nearly tripled.

Geely is among Chinese automakers turning to overseas sales to sidestep near-ruinous pricing competition at home. Cut off from the lucrative US market, much of their expansion has focused on Europe, where they’re taking share from incumbents with competitively priced EVs and hybrids. Geely also plans to expand to Canada next year.

The company’s exports surged to 323,442 vehicles in the three months through September, accounting for roughly 40% of Geely’s total sales, according to earlier company statements. But in China, billionaire Li Shufu’s auto empire has been grappling with a shrinking car market and a prolonged price war.

Business abroad is also expected to become more complicated. European Union authorities are preparing additional trade hurdles to protect local manufacturers, including a cap on hybrid-vehicle imports from China.

Negative currency exchange effects held back quarterly profit by roughly 400 million yuan, Geely said.

See also: Mercedes readies major China overhaul as slump deepens

title: Singapore’s top envoy on mission to soothe Indonesian angst
article:
(Oct 28): Singapore’s top diplomat got to Jakarta so fast this week that his hosts described the visit as unexpected.

The flight between the two Southeast Asian capitals takes less than two hours, and Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan was on a mission to quickly soothe relations that had frayed in recent weeks.

Tensions came to a head over the weekend, when Indonesia suddenly cut natural gas supplies to Singapore. The volume involved was manageable, but the abrupt move — coupled with comments by President Prabowo Subianto and members of his cabinet — appeared to send a clear message.

For Singapore, it was key to speak face-to-face. “When things happen, especially transboundary events, there’s a need for high-level direct communication between governments,” Balakrishnan told reporters Wednesday. “You can’t conduct diplomacy just by the phone or through the media.”

Officials in the city-state arranged the trip with their counterparts in Jakarta before frustrations escalated or the situation could be exploited for political purposes, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified.

The Singapore envoy met Prabowo on Wednesday afternoon, a day after holding talks with Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir. While declining to detail the conversations, Balakrishan said that Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Prabowo had been in communication.

See also: Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after fleeing Brazil — O Globo

“It sets the political commitment on both sides to do what is necessary, and now we will have to implement those plans, execute that commitment,” he said, adding that during his visit he had “good conversations, honest conversations, sincere conversations”.

At a joint press conference with his Indonesian counterpart on Tuesday, Balakrishnan stressed in Indonesian that “we may sometimes have differences of opinion, but what matters most is how we understand these differences and work together to overcome challenges”.

The conciliatory tone contrasted with increasingly pointed comments from some Indonesian officials and former officials, particularly on social media.

See also: Trump and Xi’s managed, competitive coexistence

Former trade minister Muhammad Lutfi earlier accused Singapore’s Temasek Holdings Pte Ltd and GIC Pte Ltd of pressuring MSCI Inc to consider downgrading the country’s stocks, an allegation both state-owned funds deny.

He later released a lengthy video laying out how Singapore is a conduit for Indonesia resource firms to avoid paying Indonesian taxes — the kind of resource “leakages” that Prabowo has railed against.

Communications and Digital Affairs Minister Meutya Hafid posted what appeared to be a veiled threat that Singapore could lose 80% of its internet service if connections were cut from Indonesia “whether by accident or design”.

Cabinet Secretary Teddy Indra Wijaya earlier said Balakrishnan’s had arrived “unexpectedly” and “pleaded” to meet Prabowo.

The angst followed weeks of tension over severe haze that had blanketed the region, caused mainly by land-clearing fires in Indonesia worsened by El Niño. Singapore had stepped up scrutiny of locally listed companies it said were involved.

After the two foreign ministers met Tuesday, they announced a joint taskforce to address the issue.

That outcome was important to show that both sides wanted the same things: clean air, accountability for the companies involved, and steady energy supplies, according to the people familiar with the matter. Singapore also sees Indonesia’s messaging as directed towards its domestic audience, they added.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

That pressure was on display Wednesday, when about 1,000 demonstrators gathered in separate groups around Jakarta’s Hotel Indonesia Roundabout, with some pushing through police barricades. Students protested over the forest fires, government spending priorities and civil liberties, while similar demonstrations were held in other Indonesian cities.

Back in Singapore, officials met with senior executives from 10 companies identified by the National Environment Agency as having possible links to the wildfires. Local media reported that attendees included Wilmar International chairman Kuok Khoon Hong and Franky Widjaja, a member of the family behind the Sinar Mas conglomerate, whose businesses include Asia Pulp & Paper and Golden Agri-Resources.

“We need to make sure that the companies here conduct their operations in a manner that doesn’t affect Singapore or the region,” Senior Minister K Shanmugam told reporters after the meeting. “I told them we expect full cooperation from the companies. And in the meeting, the companies said they will cooperate fully.”

Golden Agri-Resources and Asia Pulp & Paper separately confirmed that senior company representatives met with Singapore government ministers regarding transboundary haze matters.

Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu, who also attended the meeting, said Singapore’s government will propose amendments to the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act at the next parliamentary sitting. The changes will give the current framework the force of law, and “companies that do not comply will be committing an offence”, she said.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore also said it expects banks to engage with clients that may be linked to activities contributing to the haze and obtain enough information to understand their role. “Clear breaches of environmental laws would warrant stronger measures, including limiting exposures or exiting the relationship,” it said in a statement.

title: DoorDash moves earnings date forward amid Instacart deal reports
article:
(Oct 29): DoorDash Inc, the food delivery provider in talks to take over Instacart, moved its earnings release date forward by almost a week.

The company now plans to report third-quarter results before the market opens on Oct 29, rather than Nov 4 as previously planned. It didn’t give a reason for the change in its statement late Wednesday.

DoorDash is in advanced talks to acquire Instacart parent Maplebear Inc for roughly US$17 billion, people familiar with the matter said this week. A deal for the grocery app could be announced as soon as this week, said the people. No final decision has been made and discussions could fall through.

The talks come as competition intensifies in the the grocery delivery sector. Instacart previously held talks about selling itself to Uber Technologies Inc, Bloomberg News has reported.

title: Hong Kong landlords pocket 23% premiums after greening offices
article:
(Oct 29): Hong Kong landlords investing in green office refurbishments stand to pocket significantly bigger rent premiums than their counterparts in other major cities, according to a fresh analysis by property broker Savills.

Hong Kong offers average rent premiums of 23% for green upgrades, Savills calculations shared with Bloomberg show. The city is followed by Amsterdam and London, where rent premiums average 18% and 11%, respectively. In London, landlords investing in green improvements are also able to secure longer-term contracts with tenants, the analysis found.

Investments in basic energy-efficiency measures such as better insulation have taken on greater importance against a backdrop of recurring energy crises and volatile oil and gas prices. At the same time, there’s growing evidence that tenants are willing to pay more to live in buildings that use environmentally friendly materials, the Savills analysis shows.

For investors, greener buildings can be cheaper to finance and are seen as a more reliable path to preserving value, said Georgios Askounis, a director at Savills Earth. For tenants, such buildings are often associated with greater comfort and prestige, he said.

Tenants “appreciate the positive impact of being in a sustainable building, a building that’s healthier, a building that has better quality, lower energy demand, that is less likely to overheat, possibly better access to amenities,” said Askounis.

The study, which is based on an analysis of more than 2,000 office buildings, found that structures meeting criteria for at least one environmental standard consistently attracted higher rents. Savills compared rental values in Amsterdam, Chicago, New York, Hong Kong, London and Singapore and looked at the extent to which buildings in those cities adhered to the environmental standard most commonly targeted there. The analysis controlled for factors like a building’s age and size, to focus on premiums specifically linked to environmental factors.

See also: CGAC, SGX RegCo’s proposed changes to corporate governance code and listing rules include cap on directorships

In London and Amsterdam, almost all new building projects are now designed to meet high environmental standards, as regulators across Europe enforce stricter rules. Corporate tenants are also under pressure to seek out greener buildings to meet their own sustainability reporting requirements.

Businesses “want to future-proof their real estate portfolios against tightening regulation and rising energy costs,” said Askounis. Against that backdrop, many Savills clients are weighing whether to invest in costly renovations to meet the highest environmental standards, he added.

In London, buildings that meet the highest green standards — categorised as “outstanding” by Savills, can charge an extra 28% in rent with tenants staying an average of almost 10 years, the report found. Buildings judged to have “excellent” green standards — one notch lower than those deemed to be “outstanding” — were able to charge an additional 10% in rent and to hold on to tenants for almost eight years on average.

See also: Seven Singapore-listed names among ‘global sector leaders’ in annual real estate ESG benchmark

In Singapore, meanwhile, landlords investing in green refurbishments were least likely to enjoy a rent premium. That’s because the vast majority of buildings there already meet such standards, which are increasingly expected as a basic feature, Savills found.

The green rent premium was smallest in the US, where Chicago and New York only saw bumps of 6% and 7%, respectively.

“I think the certifications aren’t advertised to occupiers in the same way that they might be in Europe,” said Sarah Brooks, associate director at Savills World Research, who co-authored the analysis. In the US, green features are treated as “one small part of a broader offering.”

title: Uniqlo scraps price rise on US$2 socks after Japan shopper outcry
article:
(Oct 29): Uniqlo ditched plans to raise the price of its popular ¥290 (US$1.84) socks, underscoring the challenge Japanese retailers face as persistent inflation squeezes household budgets.

Earlier this month, the apparel brand, owned and operated by Fast Retailing Co, had announced broad price hikes for its clothing products due to rising input costs. Less than two weeks later, it reversed a decision to increase the price of its socks by ¥100 (US$0.63), and eliminate discounts on purchases of three or more pairs.

After decades of deflation, which conditioned Japanese shoppers to expect flat prices, retailers are struggling with how much of their rising costs they can pass on to customers. Consumer prices, excluding fresh food and other items, climbed 3.2% in September from a year earlier, while household spending is shrinking, reflecting the challenge companies face when seeking to protect margins.

“The fact that they decided not to go ahead with the price increase suggests they were very conscious of consumers’ resistance to higher prices,” said Atsushi Takeda, chief economist at Itochu Research Institute. “It’s no longer just lower-income consumers who are feeling the strain, but consumers somewhat higher up the income scale are also increasingly becoming wary of rising prices.”

Uniqlo’s swift response to the socks price hike followed an outcry on social media from shoppers frustrated by higher prices.

“As socks are an essential everyday item, in Japan we reconsidered our planned price revision,” a Fast Retailing spokesperson said.

title: Tech stocks drop as Alphabet, Samsung disappoint
article:
(Oct 29): Technology shares fell, snapping this week’s rally, after disappointing earnings from two industry heavyweights revived concerns about the billions of dollars companies are pouring into artificial intelligence (AI).

Samsung Electronics Co shares dropped more than 5% after profit missed estimates, dragging down the Kospi Index — a bellwether for the AI trade — by 2.9%. That marked a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when the gauge posted its biggest rally since July as strong earnings from chipmaker SK Hynix Inc fuelled gains across technology stocks.

Alphabet Inc slumped 10% in extended trading after sales underwhelmed, reinforcing investors’ fears that Google is losing ground to AI rivals despite pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology. Futures for the Nasdaq 100 Index slid 1.3%, after the underlying benchmark climbed for the past three days. The broader MSCI Inc’s Asia Pacific equities reversed earlier gains to drop 0.7%.

The news wasn’t all bad as Microsoft Corp shares rose 2.9% in after-hours trading on solid cloud sales, while Oracle Corp earlier surged 11% after issuing a long-term outlook for free cash flow. A gauge of Oracle’s credit risk improved the most in nearly nine months.

The latest earnings have exposed fresh cracks in the AI trade, raising doubts about whether massive spending on the technology can deliver returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. The concern is that investment in chips, data centres and other infrastructure is accelerating faster than the revenue needed to generate adequate returns, leaving technology shares vulnerable to further disappointment.

“The divergence in after-hours trading between Alphabet and Microsoft shares highlights growing scrutiny of how big tech companies are funding their ambitious data centre build-outs,” said Hugh Lam, a Sydney-based investment strategist at Betashares Capital Ltd.

See also: Asian stocks rise, Treasuries steady before Fed decision

Elsewhere, shorter-maturity Treasuries held their gains from Wednesday when the Federal Reserve (Fed) held off from raising interest rates, while signalling fewer policy-setting meetings next year. The yield on the rate-sensitive two-year note was at 4.69%.

Meanwhile, oil dropped as traders assessed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran. Global benchmark Brent declined 0.5% to US$114.80 a barrel.

Still, the macro backdrop offered little support for markets as renewed tensions with Iran threatened to lift oil prices, stoke inflation and reinforce the case for keeping borrowing costs elevated.

See also: Tech rally extends to Asia on Anthropic, oil falls

“The Fed appears comfortable being patient for now as financial conditions have evolved broadly in line with expectations,” said Luis Alvarado at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “But patience should not be confused with complacency.”

More central bank decisions are due this week, with the European Central Bank announcing policy Thursday and the Bank of Japan on Friday. Both are expected to keep rates unchanged.

Thursday also brings personal consumption expenditures data, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, which will offer fresh clues on price pressures in the economy.

Meanwhile, the Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold its benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%. In their post-meeting statement, policymakers said they hoped incoming data in the coming weeks would help inform their next decision.

Fed chairman Kevin Warsh said officials have “made clear our readiness to act as circumstances require, and we have shown our willingness to act”. Warsh also said the central bank will phase in an adjusted meeting schedule, with plans to hold rate-setting votes at seven out of eight meetings next year.

“Fewer decision meetings plus no forward guidance are a recipe for bigger repricing around each one, and more volatility around rates than markets are currently pricing,” said Ali Hassan, portfolio manager at Santa Fe, New Mexico-based Thornburg Investment Management.

title: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets
article:
(Oct 29): Brazil’s state-controlled oil producer Petrobras lifted production to a record and ran its refineries near full capacity in the third quarter, helping the country weather disruptions to global energy markets from the Iran war.

Oil and gas output climbed 12% on year to 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent a day, Petroleo Brasileiro SA, as the company is formally known, said in a filing on Wednesday. Production rose 5.3% compared to the second quarter as Petrobras ramped up new platforms at deep-water fields, including the P-78 and P-79 units at the giant Buzios project.

The floating production and storage vessel Alexandre de Gusmao reached peak production at the Mero field, and there were fewer losses from maintenance shutdowns, Petrobras said.

The growth in production and refining has helped Latin America’s largest economy limit its exposure to the global energy shock. Petrobras ran its refineries at 99% of capacity during the quarter, reaching record diesel production.

Oil production of 2.8 million barrels a day in the quarter puts Petrobras above its implied 2026 guidance and gives the company a higher starting point for 2027, according to Ativa Investimentos analyst Ilan Arbetman, who had flagged the potential in a note ahead of the report.

Brazil has used subsidies and tax cuts to cushion consumers from soaring fuel costs, while Petrobras has kept its refineries running at high rates to supply the domestic market.

See also: Oil jumps with Israeli election and Iran attack report in focus

But with Brent trading above US$110 a barrel and Petrobras fuel prices lagging international benchmarks, pressure is building on the company to raise prices. On Wednesday, Petrobras’s average diesel price at the refinery gate was 3.76 reais (US$0.70) a litre below import parity, a gap of 115%, according to fuel importers association Abicom. Gasoline was 24% below international levels, according to the group.

title: Alphabet’s revenue miss reignites fears over AI spending binge
article:
(Oct 29): Alphabet Inc’s search and advertising sales disappointed in the most recent quarter, reinforcing investors’ fears that Google is losing ground to artificial intelligence (AI) rivals despite pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology.

The Google parent reported sales, excluding partner payouts, of US$111.2 billion ($142.4 billion) for the third quarter, falling short of analysts’ projections. Its advertising revenue from the search engine and related businesses — which accounts for roughly half of overall sales and is critical to financing its massive AI investments — also missed forecasts, growing at the slowest pace in five quarters.

Shares of Alphabet slid 10% in late trading on Wednesday. The company’s performance stood in particularly stark contrast to rival Microsoft Corp, which reported growth in its cloud business that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations while keeping its spending in check, stoking a rally in its stock.

The pressure on Alphabet chief executive officer Sundar Pichai to justify the more than US$1 trillion that Google is facing in future payments on resources such as data centres, computing and energy to power his AI ambitions is mounting. “This quarter feels like a moment of truth for Alphabet: Either Pichai and his team fix the way the company monetizes AI, or the giant risks losing its leadership in several of its core businesses in the near future,” said Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com.

“Until Google shows it can charge for AI the way it once charged for search ads,” he said, every capital spending forecast it issues is going to “read less like ambition and more like a bill”.

See also: Memory stocks lost their shine despite strong earnings

Google’s sprint to build AI infrastructure for both itself and customers has sent the firm’s capital expenditures soaring to record levels. The firm is working to overhaul popular products such as the search engine, YouTube and Gmail with AI. But those efforts have yet to yield the kind of revenue the investors want to see to justify all the spending.

Google’s overall services revenue totalled US$96.3 billion in the third quarter, below estimates for US$98.4 billion. YouTube advertising sales of US$11.2 billion also fell below projections.

Adding to investors’ concerns: Alphabet chief business officer Philipp Schindler said in an earnings call with investors late Wednesday that the growing popularity of AI Mode, a new tab in Google Search, took a toll on the company’s results. Those queries have “lower monetization”, Schindler said, though he noted that the company was optimistic and has plans to bring more ads to that part of the search engine.

See also: Instagram ramps up video strategy in escalating TikTok, YouTube rivalry

In the meantime, Google’s AI bets are getting even more expensive. By the end of the third quarter, Google’s future commitments to buy resources such as computing power and energy totalled US$924 billion. Upcoming obligations such as data-centre leases that haven’t yet commenced hit US$152 billion, bringing the company’s total future obligations to well over US$1 trillion.

For the second quarter in a row, the company posted negative free cash flow, something it had, up until now, never seen since going public.

“Search still generates the bulk of Alphabet’s cash, and two straight quarters of negative free cash flow show the pure AI math isn’t working right now,” said Anders Bylund, contributing tech analyst at the Motley Fool.

Alphabet said in July that capital expenditures will reach as much as US$205 billion this year, more than double what it spent last year. AI requires massive amounts of computing power, and Google is racing to build data centres so it can meet demand for AI from consumers, businesses and its own employees.

Alphabet’s equity investments also weighed on the company’s bottom line. Those stakes posted an US$8.7 billion loss, in large part due to Alphabet’s SpaceX position. That’s a sharp reversal from the gains it saw a year earlier and the windfall in the second quarter that was mainly driven by SpaceX and an investment in a private company that Bloomberg later identified as Anthropic PBC.

Its third-quarter net income was US$2.12 a share, falling far below Wall Street’s estimate of US$2.99.

One bright spot in the report was Google Cloud, which is seen as a key gauge of demand for the company’s AI products and hosting services. The division reported sales of US$30.7 billion and profit of US$11.1 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of US$29.1 billion in revenue and US$9.8 billion in profit. Among the unit’s biggest customers are startups such as Anthropic that compete with Google in the AI race.

“Cloud is booming, but many of its best customers are building assistants that are already beating Google with consumers,” Monteiro wrote. “Right now, Alphabet earns more selling AI to its rivals than using it itself, and that gap should keep growing over the next few quarters unless its models change drastically, and quickly.”

Over the past few years, Google has been working to reinvent its search engine for the AI age, trying to keep consumers in the habit of relying on its answers even as chatbots from OpenAI and Anthropic become more popular. The company now delivers AI-generated answers in response to many searches, a shift that has had major implications for businesses that have traditionally relied on the search giant for traffic and advertising revenue.

Google has worked particularly hard on building an edge by generating more personalised responses to questions, leveraging years of information about its users. In recent months, though, the company has fallen behind Anthropic and OpenAI in developing AI coding tools. Google recently released Gemini 4, which it says excels in areas such as coding and cybersecurity, though some employees fear the company has yet to fully catch up.

Hours before its earnings call, Google announced yet another new AI model known as Carbon, a potential answer to the critics who’ve called for the company to speed up the pace of AI development.

“We have more models coming soon,” Pichai told analysts on the call, “including more efficient versions to help developers optimise for speed and cost and to deploy across our billions of users”.

title: Oil declines as traders parse signs of fresh diplomacy on Iran
article:
(Oct 29) : Oil dropped as traders weighed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran.

West Texas Intermediate fell toward US$102 a barrel, after rising almost 3% in the previous session, while Brent closed near US$115. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran continued to give diplomacy chance, and the Wall Street Journal reported US Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the nation’s top security body.

President Donald Trump told Axios on Wednesday that negotiations were taking place through mediators but stressed he didn’t know whether they would bear fruit. “We need to finish the job — either through a deal or another way — we will find out if negotiations can succeed,” he was quoted as saying.

Global crude benchmark Brent has rallied by 11% this month, touching the highest since April, as the conflict dragged on. The surge has heaped pressure on consumers and presented a challenge to central bankers seeking to contain inflation. While the Federal Reserve opted to keep policy unchanged this week, traders expect officials to resume tightening in December.

US voters will go to the polls on Nov. 3 for midterm elections amid signs that there’ll be a slump in support for Republicans. President Trump has given frequent signals that he may opt to resume a military campaign against Tehran after ballots have been cast, possibly in coordination with Israel’s forces.

In Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu edged ahead of opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot after a tightly fought election, although neither has a clear path toward forming a government. It will be days before President Isaac Herzog chooses who gets the chance to cobble together a new ruling coalition.

See also: Stocks edge higher after Fed as Oracle surges 11%

title: Stocks edge higher after Fed as Oracle surges 11%
article:
(Oct 29) : Stocks edged up as the Federal Reserve held rates steady and refrained from offering a clear signal on whether it will hike in December.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3%. Oracle Corp. soared 11% on a long-term outlook for free cash flow. Microsoft Corp. jumped in extended trading on solid cloud sales. Alphabet Inc. sank on disappointing results. Short-dated Treasuries gained. An oil rally waned in late hours as the Wall Street Journal said US Vice President JD Vance reached out to an Iranian hard-liner to revive peace talks.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold its benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%. In their post-meeting statement, policymakers said they hoped incoming data would help inform their next decision.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted officials have “made clear our readiness to act as circumstances require, and we have shown our willingness to act.”

“The Fed appears comfortable being patient for now as financial conditions have evolved broadly in line with expectations,” said Luis Alvarado at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “But patience should not be confused with complacency.”

Warsh also said the central bank will phase in an adjusted meeting schedule, with plans to hold rate-setting votes at seven out of eight meetings next year.

See also: Oil holds biggest gain in week as Saudi attacks fan supply risks

The Fed’s new meeting schedule appears consistent with Warsh’s push for less forward guidance and less frequent signaling to markets, according to Tony Miano at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

“The biggest change from the Fed today wasn’t to policy rates but rather to the forward calendar of making decisions,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets. “The most relevant question at the moment is what meetings will be devoted to things other than potentially changing rates.”

If nothing else, short-dated notes rose as Warsh left the market with the impression that one hike — in September — was effective thus far, Lyngen added. That would imply that following a December move, a third hike might not be seen as necessary, he noted.

See also: Asian stocks to slide on tech rout, bonds rally

While traders maintained bets officials will raise rates in December, they trimmed wagers on additional hikes in 2027. Futures markets are no longer fully pricing three more hikes this cycle.

title: Mi Material closes at $1.82 on first day of trading; Stabilisation manager bought 1.5 mil shares at IPO price of $1.80
article:
Mi Material closed at $1.82 on its first day of trading on Oct 28, valuing the company at $900 million.

Mi Material’s share price debuted at $1.80, which is equivalent to its initial public offering (IPO) price, and reached an intra-day high of $1.86. At the close of trading on Oct 28, more than 10.7 million shares changed hands.

On Oct 27, Mi Material announced that its IPO was just 2.2 times subscribed. The public offer of slightly over 6.2 million shares was just 1.3 times taken, while the international offer of nearly 71.3 million shares was 2.2 times subscribed.

Mi Material’s stabilisation manager, CGS International, has purchased 1.5 million shares at $1.80 on Oct 28. With this latest purchase, the stabilisation manager has left with just 3.5 million shares under the grant of over-allotment option.

OCBC and CGS International are the joint global coordinators, bookrunners and underwriters for this IPO.
